If the withdrawal credentials are appropriate you could perhaps push the balance directly the validator becomes withdrawable? excerpts.author: djrtwo
excerpts.content:
Hi all! As prompted by some discussion around a recent tweet by <@!273808422753796097> (https://twitter.com/VitalikButerin/status/1297676370936344576), we've added this channel to discuss the future of validator withdrawals.

In general, this will require a new `WITHDRAWAL_PREFIX` (e.g. 0x01, 0x02, ...) and specified logic on how (and where) it would be handled.

cc: <@!591364117592539137>

excerpts.author: ryg9705
excerpts.content: Do I get that right that the benefit for the end user would be that he or she can get to his or her ETH rewards in ETH 2 Phase 1.5 (The Merge) rather than ETH2 Phase 2?

excerpts.author: djrtwo
excerpts.content: no

excerpts.author: djrtwo
excerpts.content: the benefit for commiting to a contract-based withdrawal scheme today would be that people can use more sophisticated ownership models for withdrawal credentials today

excerpts.author: djrtwo
excerpts.content:
the 0x00 withdrawal prefix is just a BLS signing key.
If we commited today to a new withdrawal prefix that _will_ be honored via some predetermined mechanism on eth1 (likely the addition of an opcode to consume a wthidrawal from the beacon chain) then people could use that logic

excerpts.author: djrtwo
excerpts.content: the tough parts are (1) defining a standard today with imperfect information about the future and (2) writing an EIP in such a way that there is a social commitment to implement it on eth1 when the merge happens

excerpts.author: jgm
excerpts.content: I'd be inclined to preceed this with a "change withdrawal credentials" operation.  That would give some surety that validators can move to a smart contract-based approach without the pressure to do so at the moment they start staking.

excerpts.author: djrtwo
excerpts.content: interesting approach! trying to think if there are any security issues here

excerpts.author: djrtwo
excerpts.content: I suppose the owner of the bls key has all the power anyway so having them change the withdrawal method isn't really giving them more power

excerpts.author: djrtwo
excerpts.content: other than the power to revoke or nuance their power

excerpts.author: jgm
excerpts.content: The only concern it brings for me would be that pepole would probably use it is a back-door transfer system, and then we'd have to worry about chain rollbacks.  As such, I wouldn't suggest bringing it in right at the beginning of the chain but a little later down the line.

excerpts.author: djrtwo
excerpts.content: indeed

excerpts.author: djrtwo
excerpts.content: interesting transfer system!

excerpts.author: djrtwo
excerpts.content: I'm inclined to more concretely define this (potential) standard and assssing the risks before figuring out how it would be 'deployed' on eth2

excerpts.author: ralexstokes
excerpts.content: <@144468805697929216> how does a “chain rollback” figure in? I’d imagine operators will wait for finalized “change withdrawal credentials” operations before acting on them

excerpts.author: djrtwo
excerpts.content: emergency rollback in early days of eth2

excerpts.author: djrtwo
excerpts.content: if there are no transfers, that is much more of an option

excerpts.author: ralexstokes
excerpts.content: the concern here being that if i transfer i may just walk away from my staking concerns and then under rollback i'd not be available to continue my duty

excerpts.author: ralexstokes
excerpts.content: whereas w/o transfers my stake holds me accountable for the foreseeable future

excerpts.author: djrtwo
excerpts.content: no, the concern being that a rollback could essentially trigger a double spend

excerpts.author: djrtwo
excerpts.content: or undo some sort of user to user tx

excerpts.author: ralexstokes
excerpts.content: ahok

excerpts.author: ajsutton
excerpts.content:
If changing withdrawal credentials was used as a transfer mechanism you'd likely wind up with two people having the signing keys then.  And the original owner would no longer have anything at stake.
Potentially works for custodial staking services though.

excerpts.author: jgm
excerpts.content: And non-custodial staking services, but yes it wouldn't work if the original owner held both keys.

excerpts.author: djrtwo
excerpts.content: seems like more of  a viable strategy for exited vals

excerpts.author: djrtwo
excerpts.content: hmm

excerpts.author: jgm
excerpts.content: The primary purpose of my suggestion was to allow someone to change their withdrawal method, so if it doesn't work for transfers I don't see that being a significant downside

excerpts.author: djrtwo
excerpts.content: right

excerpts.author: jgm
excerpts.content: (Been thinking about this a bit, there are fair few wrinkles in allowing withdrawal to a smart contract, or in general to an ETH1 address.  A lot depends on how ETH2 finalizes ETH1; do we have any docs with current thinking on this?)

excerpts.author: djrtwo
excerpts.content: in the phase 1.5, eth2 just builds eth1 chain as a shard. it is first crosslinked into the beacon chain and then finalized

excerpts.author: djrtwo
excerpts.content: eth1 will have access to "system" level opcodes about the beacon chain

excerpts.author: djrtwo
excerpts.content: from there, you could imagine a TX that "consumes" a validator that is "withdrawable" and has the special `0x01` prefix into the specified contract

excerpts.author: djrtwo
excerpts.content: the accounting on triggering that "consumption" back to the beacon chain might be tricky..

excerpts.author: djrtwo
excerpts.content: yes things to think through

excerpts.author: djrtwo
excerpts.content: standard BLS withdrawals will need this thought through to a certain extent as well

excerpts.author: jgm
excerpts.content:
Thanks.  I'd assume that the BLS withdrawals would be some sort of (ETH1 address, BLS signature from withdrawal key) operation.

If the withdrawal credentials are appropriate you could perhaps push the balance directly the validator becomes withdrawable?  If we aren't going to allow recycling of withdrawable Ether in to new validators it seems like the manual withdrawal is an unnecessary step (unless we have a good reason to keep the withdrawable Ether sitting in the validator until the smart contract asks for it).

excerpts.author: djrtwo
excerpts.content:
> I'd assume that the BLS withdrawals would be some sort of (ETH1 address, BLS signature from withdrawal key) operation.
yes, it'd have to be. but at the same time, the eth1 shard chain needs to be able to prevent "double withdrawals" and maintain some sort of bitfield or other data structure to remember consumption of a withdrawal

excerpts.author: djrtwo
excerpts.content:
>  push the balance
This is possible, but would need a max per block if it were an auto system operation instead of a gas-limited operation
